verdict_reason: Mechanically the config is correct and idiomatic (a Jackson2ObjectMapperBuilderCustomizer, so Boot's JavaTimeModule and problemdetails wiring survive), but the naming strategy it sets — LOWER_CAMEL_CASE — puts the shipped wire format in direct conflict with the repo's own committed snake_case api-contract.locked.yaml and the rest-api best practice, and the compliance IT's divergence gate does not catch it

todos.issue: propertyNamingStrategy(LOWER_CAMEL_CASE) makes the whole HTTP boundary camelCase (addressLine1, townOrCity, traceId), directly contradicting the committed docs/openapi/api-contract.locked.yaml, which mandates snake_case JSON properties throughout (address_line_1, created_at, organisation_id, and trace_id described there as 'a deliberate divergence from the animals-backend camelCase'), and the rest-api best practice ('snake_case for properties', 'Don't: camelCase in JSON'); OperatorComplianceIT's divergence gate only compares paths/HTTP methods/operationIds, so the property-name reversal passes CI unnoticed
todos.fix: Pick one and make it explicit: either drop this customizer (or switch to PropertyNamingStrategies.SNAKE_CASE plus @JsonProperty for the address_line_1 style names SNAKE_CASE cannot derive) to honour the locked contract, or reissue/retire api-contract.locked.yaml as camelCase with the decision recorded, and extend the compliance IT's divergence gate to compare component-schema property names so the two can never silently disagree again

todos.issue: The customizer pins two contract-visible Jackson knobs (naming, unknown properties) but leaves date/time serialisation to the Spring Boot default, and no test asserts it: OperatorResponse exposes Instant createdAt/modifiedAt which the contract declares as RFC 3339 date-time strings, yet OperatorComplianceIT only asserts jsonPath('$.createdAt').exists() — a later spring.jackson.serialization.write-dates-as-timestamps=true would silently turn them into epoch numbers with a green build
todos.fix: Either add .featuresToDisable(SerializationFeature.WRITE_DATES_AS_TIMESTAMPS) here to pin the behaviour explicitly alongside the other two knobs, or tighten OperatorComplianceIT to assert createdAt/modifiedAt match an ISO-8601 instant pattern rather than merely existing
